events.title: Feodor III becomes Tsar of Russia
events.description: On the death of Tsar Alexei, his sickly 14-year-old son Feodor succeeded him. In a short reign he abolished the system of ranking nobles by ancestry, paving the way for his half-brother Peter the Great.

events.title: George III dies at Windsor
events.description: Blind and suffering from mental illness, George III died after a reign of almost 60 years, which had seen the loss of America and victory over Napoleon. His son the Prince Regent became George IV.

events.title: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Raven' is published
events.description: Poe's poem of a grieving lover and a talking bird appeared in the New York Evening Mirror. It made him famous almost overnight, though it earned him little money.
events.html: Poe's poem of a grieving lover and a talking bird appeared in the New York Evening Mirror. It made him famous almost overnight, though it earned him little money.

events.title: Karl Benz files a patent for his motor car
events.description: Benz applied for a German patent on a 'vehicle powered by a gas engine', his three-wheeled Motorwagen. It is generally regarded as the first practical petrol-driven automobile.

events.title: The American League of baseball is organised
events.description: Ban Johnson reorganised a minor league as the American League, with eight teams. It declared itself a major league in 1901 and met the National League in the first World Series in 1903.

events.title: Zeppelin raid kills civilians in Paris
events.description: A German airship bombed eastern Paris, killing more than twenty people in the Ménilmontant area. It was the last Zeppelin raid on the city, which strengthened its air defences.
